evidence.note: Profiled and diagnosed permute+contiguous (17ms×2) as the true perf bottleneck, then abandoned the permute-based design for a strided/Triton approach — root-causing a slow path rather than tweaking constants.
Triton bmm gave a big speedup but produced NaNs; agent diagnosed out-of-bounds from N not being a block multiple and added bounds checking — correcting a wrong intermediate, not the tolerance.

Repeatedly traced Cauchy tolerance misses to bf16 precision loss on heavy-tailed inputs (quantifying failure counts and allclose semantics) and reverted the bf16 casts, cleanly distinguishing numeric failure from the perf motive.
Distinguished correctness vs latency, autotuned LN and fused_final per-shape (7ms→2.1ms LN), re-verifying correctness after each fix without regressing prior wins.
Extended circling on proj5/final autotune configs producing washes; knew to stop optimizing small shapes but never root-caused the residual ~13% gap, keeping this short of the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent consistently distinguishes correctness failures from performance failures and root-causes each — Cauchy tolerance misses traced to bf16 precision, NaNs traced to missing bounds checks, slow shapes traced to permute/tiling — then revises the design and re-verifies without regressing (matching anchor 8). It revisits earlier decisions (reverting fusions, streams, bf16 weights) and focuses only on the two bottleneck shapes. It falls short of 10 because the late trajectory devolves into repeated micro-tweak autotuning that mostly washes, and it never root-causes the persistent latency gap.
